Definition: to abrade, i.e. harrow a field
BiblicalUsage: The sense of sâdad is to abrade, that is harrow a field. It stands in Hosea 10:11, "And Ephraim an heifer taught, loveth to tread…", and in Isaiah 28:24, "Doth the plowman plow all day to sow?…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God put sâdad here on purpose, and I take his word for it.
